home.title:
A place to rest,
not to stay.
home.subtitle: Not a hotel, not a motel, not a hostel. RESTEL is a Korean rest space you rent by the hour. Take off your shoes, step up onto the wooden platform, and find floor mats and blankets, soft light, and a warm cup of tea waiting.

notHotel.title: You don't check in. You come in to rest.
notHotel.body: RESTEL isn't somewhere to spend the night. Whether it's one hour or half a day, you rent the whole atmosphere you need to rest: folding mats and a sofa instead of beds, blankets instead of duvets, a quiet entrance instead of a check-in. It's the fourth kind of "-tel", built around rest.

about.title: What is RESTEL
about.lead: RESTEL joins REST and TEL. After the hotel, the motel and the hostel comes a new kind of "-tel": a place you enter to rest.
story: Hotels grew out of service and formality, motels out of the road trip, hostels out of backpacker culture. The suffix "-tel" no longer describes a building; it describes a way of staying.

Koreans rest on the floor. On a warm ondol floor with a mat rolled out, in a grandmother's room, on the wooden deck of a jjimjilbang, in the open hall of a hanok. You don't need a bed to rest, and one floor can be shared by family and friends. RESTEL brings this old habit into the middle of the city.

There are no beds at RESTEL. There are folding mats and a sofa, blankets and pillows. It is not a place to spend the night but a place to rest properly, for an hour or for half a day. That is why RESTEL is a rest space rental and not an accommodation — and we say so up front.

krest.title: K-REST — Korean rest
krest.lead: For travellers, RESTEL is a way to experience how Koreans rest. We picked the parts people find unfamiliar or curious, and kept them short.

ondol.title: Ondol & floor culture
ondol.summary: Why Koreans rest on the floor
ondol.body: Ondol is Korea's traditional heated floor. A warm floor naturally invites people to sit and lie down, and it shaped a culture of sleeping, eating and resting on the floor without beds. RESTEL's raised wooden platform carries this floor culture into the city. The moment you step up without shoes, your body sits lower and your breathing slows.

yo.title: Mats, blankets & pillows
yo.summary: A mat instead of a yo, a blanket instead of a duvet
yo.body: A traditional Korean bed is a yo (padded mat) laid on the floor and a duvet on top. Because RESTEL is a space for rest, not sleepovers, we use folding mats and blankets. The buckwheat-hull pillow is a Korean classic: cool, firm, and quietly rustling when you move.

jjimjilbang.title: The jjimjilbang way of resting
jjimjilbang.summary: Resting on a shared wooden floor
jjimjilbang.body: A jjimjilbang is a Korean bathhouse where people lie down on a wide heated floor after bathing, with baked eggs, sweet rice punch and a towel folded into 'sheep ears'. RESTEL reinterprets that floor rest as private and quiet. Pair it with a bathhouse visit and your day of rest is complete.

tea.title: A cup of tea
tea.body: Korean tea isn't only leaf tea. Everyday favourites are made from grains and fruit: jujube tea simmered for hours, nutty roasted barley tea, green tea blended with roasted brown rice. The RESTEL tea corner has all three and a few small sweets, with a card showing how to brew each.

stillness.title: Stillness & meditation
stillness.body: In Korea's mountain temples a day passes with dawn chanting, 108 bows and tea talk. RESTEL distils that quiet into 10- and 20-minute guided meditations you can play through the room speaker in several languages. Counting your breath is enough.

hanok.title: The lines of a hanok
hanok.summary: A roof-tile ridge and a moon gate
hanok.body: Along the wall of RESTEL Sinchon runs a line of black roof tiles, and in the centre an arched niche shaped like a moon holds a soft glow. It's a modern compression of the hanok roofline and gate. It makes a lovely photo, but better still: lie down facing the light.

guide.title: How to rest at RESTEL
guide.lead: From entering to leaving — everything you need. The QR code inside the space opens this page too.

blocks.title: Entering
blocks.text: Open the door with the code we sent you. It works from 10 minutes before your start until 10 minutes after the end.
blocks.detail: If the door doesn't open, message the contact in your confirmation. If the building has a separate entrance code, it is included there.

blocks.title: Shoes off
blocks.text: Put your shoes in the cabinet by the door. The platform is for bare feet or socks.
blocks.detail: A hand-washing spot and sanitiser are by the entrance.

blocks.title: Light
blocks.text: Use the wall switch to choose bright, soft or dark.
blocks.detail: Ten minutes before the end, the lights slowly brighten — that's your alarm.

blocks.title: Sound
blocks.text: Nature sounds play through the speaker. Switch to silence or another channel if you like.
blocks.detail: Guided meditation plays from the player on this page or through the speaker.

blocks.title: Mats
blocks.text: Unfold a mat and take a blanket and pillow. One mat per person.
blocks.detail: Mat covers are changed every session. Drop used covers in the box by the door.

blocks.title: Tea
blocks.text: Fill a cup with hot water from the dispenser in the tea corner and steep a tea bag.
blocks.detail: Jujube, barley or brown-rice green tea. Leave used cups in the sink.

blocks.title: Quiet
blocks.text: The walls are thin. Please take calls on the terrace.
blocks.detail: Keep speaker volume at 3 or below; use earphones for videos.

blocks.title: Emergency
blocks.text: The extinguisher and emergency light are next to the door. Check the evacuation map.
blocks.detail: Emergency: 119. For anything else, use the contact in your confirmation.

blocks.title: Leaving
blocks.text: Sort your rubbish, fold the mats back, and set the lights to bright.
blocks.detail: Lost items are kept for 7 days. A one-line note about your rest means a lot to us.

items.q: Is RESTEL a hotel or hostel?
items.a: No. RESTEL is a rest space you rent by the hour. We don't provide rooms with beds and bathrooms, and there are no overnight products. Every session ends before midnight.
Yes — napping is welcome. Folding mats, blankets and a wake-up light are ready. What we don't offer is a place to spend the night.

items.q: How many people can use a space?
items.a: Prices cover two people. You can add people up to the space's maximum (6 at Sinchon) for a small fee each.
Of course. The site is in seven languages and we confirm requests by email. We're preparing payment with internationally issued cards.
Guests must be 19 or older. Whether minors may join with a guardian is announced per space.
RESTEL Sinchon has a washbasin but no shower. RESTEL is a place to rest, not somewhere to wash and sleep.
Send a request and we'll check availability and message you (email or KakaoTalk). Once payment is complete, we send your entry code.
100% refund up to 48 hours before the start, 50% up to 24 hours before, no refund after that. Changes are free before confirmation.
Light snacks and drinks are fine. Please avoid cooking, alcohol and strong-smelling food.

items.q: Can I list my own space on RESTEL?
items.a: Yes. Apply on the host page. We share the RESTEL standard (lighting, blackout, mats, signage, safety) and list your space once approved.

terms: RESTEL (the "Service") rents rest spaces by the hour and is not an accommodation business. Guests may use the space only during the booked session.
Guests must be 19 or older and must not exceed the maximum number of people for the space.
Smoking, cooking, alcohol, loud noise and behaviour that disturbs others are prohibited. Violations may end the session without refund.
Damage to the space or its contents may be charged at the cost of restoration.
The Service uses your contact details to confirm requests, send entry information and follow up after your visit.
These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Korea.
privacy: We collect: name, phone or email, preferred language, country (optional) and notes. We never collect passport or ID numbers.
Purpose: confirming and managing requests, entry information, follow-up surveys and replying to enquiries.
Retention: one year after the session, then anonymised. Transaction records required by law are kept for the statutory period.
Processors: payment provider, messaging and email providers, hosting (Cloudflare). This list is updated here when it changes.
You may request access, correction or deletion at any time using the contact details below.
refund: Cancel up to 48 hours before the start: 100% refund
Cancel up to 24 hours before the start: 50% refund
Later cancellation or no-show: no refund
Before confirmation, requests can be changed or cancelled freely.
If we cannot provide the session, you receive a full refund.
